owner_posts.post_text:
Six months. One mission. A lot of quiet, hard work.

5,700+ trees planted. 2,000+ solar lamps lighting up homes after dark. 400+ solar street lights making streets safer at night. 500+ bicycles handed out for an easier commute to school and work. 12+ classrooms rebuilt for kids who deserve better walls to learn in. One ambulance now saving lives every single day. 35+ people out of their cars for our first-ever zero emission ride.

This is what showing up, again and again, actually looks like.

First half of the year, done. Second half, let's go.

We're proud to share that 35+ members of the ThoughtSpot team came together to be part of this school beautification initiative, bringing colour and care to the school's walls.
Our heartfelt gratitude to every volunteer who gave their time and energy, and to the school for welcoming us so warmly throughout the day.

Being part of this experience meant a great deal to us, and we're thankful for the opportunity to contribute to a space where children learn and grow.

They came to colour a school's walls. Somewhere between the first brushstroke and the last, they found their own inner child again.

Grateful to the @thoughtspot volunteers who showed up with full hearts and paint-covered hands.

Turns out some "work days" don't feel like work at all.

Today the world remembers the environment. We never forgot.

Marpu doesn't live for one green day a year. Every day, every hour, our volunteers choose the planet first.

They ask for nothing back, and that is exactly what makes them the gift this earth keeps unwrapping.

The environment doesn't need a date on the calendar. It needs people who stayed.

🌱

Light for a Sustainable Future.

A reminder that 2026 is also the International Year of Volunteers for
Sustainable Development.

Both ideas anchor the same truth. Communities don't change because of
funding alone. They change because of the people who show up,
year after year, with curiosity and care.

Marpu Foundation. 23+ states. 250+ corporate partners. Over a million
volunteers and counting.

This isn't a CSR checkbox. It's what it looks like when companies actually show up.

Every frame is an employee. Engineers planting trees. Analysts painting classrooms. Managers reviving wetlands. Coders assembling solar lamps for kids who'd never had study light.
250+ corporate partners. A million people who decided their workday belonged to something larger.

Marpu doesn't run CSR drives. We run the kind your team will still talk about in the Monday standup.

Want yours in the next reel? Let's talk →

Every breath matters clean air is essential for a healthy life.

This World Asthma Day, let’s raise awareness about how pollution affects respiratory health.

A cleaner environment means fewer struggles for those living with asthma.

Small actions like reducing pollution and planting trees can create lasting impact.

Join Marpu Foundation in building a future where everyone can breathe freely. 🌿

Seed balls are one of the simplest reforestation tools, and one of the oldest.

What is a seed ball?

→ A small ball of clay, compost, and native seeds
→ Scattered across degraded land
→ Breaks open with the first rain, and the seedling grows

Why does it work?

→ Native seeds match the local ecosystem
→ The clay shell protects from birds, ants, and harsh sun
→ The compost feeds the seedling through its first weeks
→ Reaches land that conventional plantation cannot

Why does it count under CSR?

→ Aligned with Schedule VII activity 4: environmental sustainability and conservation of natural resources
→ Feeds directly into BRSR Core biodiversity disclosure
→ Hands-on, trackable, and CSR-2 documentation ready

Aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals:

→ SDG 13: Climate Action
→ SDG 15: Life on Land
→ SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals

To organise a seed ball session for your team, school, or community, write to connect@marpu.org or visit

In underserved schools across India, children sit in classrooms with no books, no libraries, no windows to the world beyond their walls.

A single book can open that window.
This World Book Day, let's bring the gift of reading to those who need it most.

The programmes that last aren't the most expensive they're the ones built with communities, not just for them.

That's the creativity this UN observance calls for. That's the innovation sustainable development demands.

name: Apnalaya
description:
Founded in Mumbai in 1973, Apnalaya is a community development NGO in Mumbai that works with the urban poor — enabling access to essential services such as healthcare, education, livelihoods, and social protection; empowering individuals and communities to organize, lead, and help themselves; and ensuring civic entitlements through continuous advocacy and collaboration with government systems.
For over five decades, Apnalaya has been building inclusive and resilient communities across Chembur, Govandi, and Mumbai’s informal settlements. Through programs on maternal and child health, disability inclusion, women empowerment, and civic rights, we work to create an equitable city where every citizen can live with dignity and opportunity.

owner_posts.post_text:
Building Sanitation Awareness Through Community Participation 🧼

Apnalaya conducted sanitation awareness programmes across Golibar, Santacruz, and Dnyaneshwar Nagar in Bandra, bringing together community members, youth, and volunteers through interactive and participatory sessions.

The programmes created space for open dialogue, where residents raised questions around sanitation and hygiene that were addressed through discussion and shared learning. These conversations helped simplify key messages, strengthen understanding, and encourage healthier practices at the community level.

Youth participation — including volunteers from initiatives such as Bright Future — added energy and leadership to the sessions. Their engagement reflected growing awareness and confidence in taking responsibility for community health and sanitation.

Together, these conversations reinforced the importance of collective responsibility in improving sanitation practices, preventing illness, and strengthening neighbourhood wellbeing.

At Apnalaya, a community development NGO in Mumbai, we continue to work alongside communities to build sustainable, people-led solutions for sanitation and public health. 🌿

👉 Learn more about our community-led work at our website.

From Orientation to Field: Learning with Communities 🌿

As part of Apnalaya Inspires, we recently hosted a learning and dialogue engagement in partnership with Dasra, bringing organisational perspective and community realities into one shared space.

The engagement began with an orientation session at the Apnalaya office, where participants were introduced to the organisation’s vision, values, programme approach, and long-term outlook. This set the context for understanding Apnalaya’s rights-based, community-led work in Mumbai’s informal settlements.

The learning then moved to the field, with a visit to Qureshi Nagar, Kurla, at the Citizenship and Advocacy Programme Community Resource Centre (CRC). Here, participants engaged directly with on-ground realities and gained insight into Apnalaya’s work on citizenship, access to civic entitlements, and collective community action.

Discussions highlighted how community collectivisation enables residents to navigate complex public systems, address gaps in basic services, and strengthen local leadership. Drawing on programme experience and research — including insights from Apnalaya’s 10-Ward Study — the dialogue reflected on what sustained, community-driven change looks like in dense urban contexts.

The engagement reaffirmed the value of learning that connects research, organisational practice, and lived experience — essential for building inclusive and resilient cities.

What Does Freedom Look Like in the City?
Access. Dignity. Voice. ⚖️

In Mumbai, freedom is practised when communities can prove who they are, access public services, and speak up without fear. In 2024–25, Apnalaya worked alongside communities to help turn constitutional rights into everyday realities.

Identity Is the First Step to Freedom

📌 6,228 individuals supported to access public systems
📌 4,877 people secured Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN, and Ration Cards
📌 1,351 households enrolled in social protection schemes

When Communities Act, Cities Respond

💧⚡🗑️ 3,376 household-level complaints raised (water, electricity, waste)
🏘️ 306 community-level civic actions led by Civic Action Groups (CAGs)
👨‍👩‍👧 16,165 families gained improved access to basic services
🌆 68,062 individuals benefited from restored infrastructure

Democracy Begins in the Neighbourhood

🙌 2,528 trained community volunteers led civic action
🤝 111 Civic Action Groups formed and strengthened
⭐ 169 community champions trained across wards

Young Citizens, Stronger Cities

🧑‍🎓 981 adolescents engaged in civic education
🗺️ Youth trained to map issues, file complaints, and engage authorities

At Apnalaya, a community development NGO in Mumbai, we believe freedom grows when communities understand systems and act collectively. When people lead, cities listen.

We are pleased to share that Apnalaya’s work has been published by the Indian School of Development Management (ISDM) in the DoDM Compendium 2024 – Development Management in Practice, Volume 1.

The chapter, titled “Empowering Urban Slum Communities through Collectivization: A Case Study of Civic Engagement in Mumbai’s M-East Ward,” documents Apnalaya’s long-term, grassroots work in Mumbai’s M-East Ward and examines how collectivisation enables sustained civic engagement in contexts marked by deprivation and fragmentation.

Authored by Amrapali Mukherjee, Kamakshi Balasubramanian, and Shachi Phadke, the study highlights collectivisation as a powerful, replicable strategy for strengthening urban governance, citizen agency, and equitable development. It offers practice-rooted evidence of how community-led, rights-based approaches can create durable systems change in informal settlements.

This publication adds to the growing body of knowledge on urban inclusion and participatory governance, reinforcing Apnalaya’s commitment as a community development NGO in Mumbai to bridging lived experience, evidence, and policy.

🔗 Access the book on the ISDM website

Community Leaders Engage in Conversations on Girls’ Rights 🌸

Apnalaya’s community leaders recently represented the organisation at the Kishori Mela, organised by @preranaantihumantrafficking — a vibrant platform for dialogue, learning, and access to services centred on girls’ rights and adolescent empowerment.

Facilitated by Dipa Ma’am, the session opened up meaningful conversations on the challenges faced by girls and women, prevailing social norms, and the role that individuals and communities play in creating safer, more supportive environments. Participants were also introduced to key rights guaranteed under the Indian Constitution, strengthening awareness of dignity, equality, and protection.

Apnalaya set up an awareness stall at the mela, engaging adolescents and community members on children’s, girls’, and women’s constitutional rights. Through open conversations and information-sharing, the stall encouraged confidence, awareness, and collective responsibility.

Spaces like the Kishori Mela are vital for nurturing informed, empowered young people who can claim their rights and shape a more equal future.

At Apnalaya, a community development NGO in Mumbai, we continue to work alongside communities to strengthen girls’ leadership, rights awareness, and inclusion. 🌿

👉 Learn more about our work

Freedom isn’t just celebrated. It’s practised. 🇮🇳

This Republic Day, Apnalaya honours the everyday acts of freedom that often go unnoticed —
being recognised,
being heard,
and claiming public services with dignity.

In neighbourhoods and communities across Mumbai, freedom comes alive when people understand their rights, navigate systems, and participate actively in civic life. Real change begins not in institutions alone, but with informed citizens and collective action.

At Apnalaya, a community development NGO in Mumbai, we work alongside communities to strengthen civic awareness, access to entitlements, and people-led change — because constitutional values matter most when they are lived every day.

Wishing everyone a Happy Republic Day. 🌿
👉 Follow us to see how communities practise freedom by claiming their civic entitlements.

National Girl Child Day | 24 January 2026 👧💙

The progress of our cities depends on how we support, protect, and invest in girls.

In Mumbai’s informal settlements, girls often face layered challenges — limited access to education, gaps in healthcare and nutrition, early caregiving responsibilities, and restricted opportunities to learn and lead. These are not individual shortcomings, but systemic barriers that require collective solutions.

At Apnalaya, we work alongside communities to address these inequities by strengthening education pathways, supporting adolescent health and nutrition, and creating safe, enabling environments where girls can grow with confidence, dignity, and agency.

Investing in girls is not only a social responsibility — it is essential for building healthier families, resilient communities, and more equitable cities.

On National Girl Child Day, we reaffirm our commitment as a community development NGO in Mumbai to ensuring that every girl has the opportunity to learn, thrive, and shape her own future. 🌿

Citizenship isn’t just a status. It’s a skillset. ⚖️

In Mumbai’s informal settlements, a missing document is never just paperwork.
A missing ration card means food insecurity.
A missing birth certificate can block a child from entering school.

That’s why at Apnalaya, we don’t only advocate for rights — we teach the mechanics of claiming them.

On 10 January, 46 community volunteers from Kamla Nagar and Kokri Agar participated in a hands-on legal learning session at the Legal Cell, SNDT College, under the mentorship of Adv. Dishad. Together, they unpacked the myths and confusion surrounding legal documentation and civic entitlements.

Volunteers learned how ration cards function as tools for food security, the municipal processes for correcting document errors, and how free legal aid can be accessed when citizens know where and how to approach the system.

Today, these volunteers return to their neighbourhoods not just as residents, but as community paralegal resources — guiding neighbours, reducing fear, and strengthening access to rights.

At Apnalaya, a community development NGO in Mumbai, we believe that when people understand the system, they gain the power to change their reality.

Look at how bright we shined 🌟

Every face here carries a story — of hope, service, and quiet courage. From Govandi to Kandivali, from Baiganwadi to Shivaji Nagar, these volunteers are the light that keeps communities moving forward every day.

Because of you, 1,84,973 lives felt supported this year.
Because of you, the distance between survival and dreams grew smaller. 💛

Through health support, education, livelihoods, civic action, and care, your commitment helped strengthen families and neighbourhoods across Mumbai’s informal settlements. You showed us that real change doesn’t always arrive loudly — it often comes through consistent presence, compassion, and collective action.

At Apnalaya, a community development NGO in Mumbai, we are deeply grateful to every volunteer who chose to stand beside communities, listen deeply, and lead with empathy.

Thank you for choosing compassion.
Thank you for being the light.

🕯️ And many more lights continue to shine…

She didn’t just find a livelihood — she reclaimed her identity. 🌿

Rubina Khan, a mother of seven from Adarsh Nagar, once ran a small snack stall, stretching every rupee to make ends meet. Like many women in Mumbai’s informal settlements, her world was defined by unpaid care and domestic responsibilities, leaving little space for dignity or choice.

At Apnalaya, we believe that when you invest in a woman, you invest in an entire community. Rubina joined a Mahila Bachat Gat (Self-Help Group) and later trained as a Community Childcare Centre (CCC) partner, gaining skills in nutrition, early childhood development, and basic business management.

Today, Rubina runs a childcare centre from her home — a safe, nurturing space for young children in her neighbourhood. But the impact goes far beyond one centre. Because Rubina opens her door each morning, seven other mothers are free to step out and work, strengthening their families’ incomes and independence.

Rubina is not just a caregiver. She is an economic engine — the Light of Solidarity that holds communities together.
“Running the CCC gave me dignity,” she says. “Now, I guide others.”

This festive season, stand with Apnalaya, a community development NGO in Mumbai, and celebrate the women who are shaping the future of our city’s children through livelihoods, care, and leadership. 🌟

featured_reviews.review_text: Volunteering with Ashish Foundation gave me a deeper understanding of the power of collective efforts in making a difference. I am truly grateful for the opportunity to contribute and highly recommend anyone looking to volunteer to join this amazing initiative.
